questionsToConsider: Which systems does everyone get by default, and which need a specific request?
Who can approve admin access, and does the form need to name them?
How much notice does IT need before a start date?
Should HR or the hiring manager be the one filling this in?
guide.howToUseResponses: Sort requests by start date so the earliest starters are set up first, and aim to finish a few days before day one. Hold any admin request where the manager hasn't approved yet and follow up with the requester. Keep the end dates for contractors and temporary staff in a calendar, since the most common access mistake is an account nobody switched off.
customizeSteps: Replace the system list with the tools your company actually runs, grouped the way IT provisions them.
Edit the department list to match your organisation chart.
Share the link with HR and hiring managers, and add it to your hiring checklist so it goes out when an offer is signed.

faqs.q: What should a new user request form include?
faqs.a: The new person's name, role, department and start date, the systems and access level they need, and their equipment. For contractors, add an end date so access can be removed on time.

faqs.q: Who should fill in a new user access request?
faqs.a: Usually the hiring manager or HR, since the new person has no accounts yet. The form asks for the requester's details separately from the new user's.

faqs.q: How do I handle admin access requests?
faqs.a: Ask for a reason and a manager's approval before granting it. This form only asks those questions when admin access is selected, so standard requests stay short.

faqs.q: Can I use this for access changes, not just new starters?
faqs.a: Yes. Copy it with Use this template and change the greeting and first questions; the systems and access questions work the same for someone changing roles.

doc.title: New user request
doc.description: Ask for accounts, access and equipment for a new starter in one go.

blocks.title: Setting up access for someone new? This takes about three minutes.
First, who is making the request?
What is the new user's full name?
Which department will they be in?
What kind of role is it?
When should their access end?
blocks.description: We'll switch accounts off on this date unless you tell us otherwise.

blocks.title: What level of access do they need?
Which systems need admin access, and why does the role need it?
Has their manager approved the admin access?
Is there a colleague whose access they should match?
blocks.description: Often the quickest way to get it right. Leave blank if not.

blocks.title: Anything else IT should know?
blocks.description: For example, they work remotely and need equipment posted.

endings.title: Request logged
endings.bodyMd: IT will confirm by email once the accounts are ready. If you asked for admin access, that part waits until the manager has approved it.

closeRules.closedMessageMd: This form is no longer accepting responses.
